purpose: Sapropterin is used to help lower high levels of phenylalanine, an amino acid, in the blood for people who have a condition called phenylketonuria (PKU). It works best in patients whose bodies can still respond to this type of treatment. It is used along with a special low-phenylalanine diet, not as a replacement for it.
how_it_works: Your body needs a natural substance called BH4 to break down phenylalanine from the foods you eat. In PKU, this process does not work properly, so phenylalanine builds up in the blood and can harm the brain. Sapropterin is a man-made version of BH4 that helps the enzyme responsible for breaking down phenylalanine work better, lowering the levels in your blood.
common_side_effects: Headache, runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, diarrhea, vomiting, cough, and stomach pain are the most commonly reported side effects. These are usually mild.
warnings: This medication does not work for everyone with PKU — your doctor will test your response after a few weeks. Keep following your special low-phenylalanine diet even while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with sapropterin. Blood phenylalanine levels must be checked regularly to make sure the medicine is working safely.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg per kg of your body weight taken once daily with a meal. Your doctor may adjust the dose based on how your phenylalanine levels respond. The tablets can be dissolved in water or apple juice to make them easier to swallow, and the dose should be taken at the same time each day.
